textbookText: 7. What happens to balloon filled with air, when it goes very high altitude from surface of earth? Why?
Ans:- When a balloon filled with air rises to a very high altitude, it expands and may eventually burst. This happens because
as the balloon goes higher, the air pressure outside decreases, while the air inside the balloon remains at a higher pressure.
The higher internal pressure pushes outward, causing the balloon to stretch. If the balloon stretches beyond its limit, the
material can no longer hold it, and the balloon bursts.
8. The ship can carry more load in ocean than in a river. Why?
Ans:- A ship can carry more load in the ocean than in a river because the density of seawater is higher than that of river
(fresh) water. The higher density of seawater increases the buoyant force acting on the ship, allowing it to float even when it
carries more weight. In fresh water, the buoyant force is less, so the ship cannot carry as much load without sinking.
9. Write two daily applications of Archimedes principle.
Ans:-Two daily applications of Archimedes’ principle are:
1. Ship floating on water: Large ships float because the buoyant force from water supports their weight.
2. Hydrometer measuring liquid density: A hydrometer floats at different levels in liquids depending on their density, using
the buoyant force.

11. What will be the effect in the weight of displaced water if load in added into the ship floating in the ocean? Witte with
reason.
Ans:- If a load is added to a ship floating in the ocean, the weight of the displaced water increases. This is because, according
to Archimedes’ principle, a floating ship displaces an amount of water equal to its total weight. When the ship’s weight
increases due to the added load, it must displace more water to remain afloat.

16. A special type of oil is used in hydraulic brakes. Why?
Ans:- A special type of oil is used in hydraulic brakes because it is incompressible and has a high boiling point. Being
incompressible ensures that the force applied on the brake pedal is efficiently transmitted to the brake pads, and a high
boiling point prevents the oil from vaporizing under high temperatures, ensuring the brakes work reliably.
